mainTopic: How a 6×6 ערוגה can hold five species without violating כלאים: the reliability of the Sages' agricultural tradition, the size of the bed and its borders, and where the bed is located
overview: The גמרא gives the reason the משנה allows five species in one 6×6 ערוגה: the Sages have a tradition that five seeds in six טפחים do not draw nourishment from one another. It then asks why we may rely on such a tradition. רבי יוחנן answers with the פסוק 'לא תסיג גבול רעך אשר גבלו ראשונים', which tells us not to move the limits set by earlier generations. Those early ones are identified as the children of שעיר החורי, who were experts in which land suits which crop, and the גמרא adds wordplays on the names חורי and חוי. The גמרא then fixes the size of the bed. רב אסי, supported by a ברייתא, says the six טפחים are the inside only, and the borders are added on top. Following רבי יהודה and the פסוק 'והשקית ברגלך', each border is one טפח wide. Finally רב limits the משנה to a bed standing alone in a חורבה, and the גמרא questions this from the empty corners and from the open space outside the bed, a challenge that is answered on the next amud.

steps.title: Five seeds in six handbreadths do not feed off each other
steps.stepSummary: The Sages have a tradition that five species planted within a six-טפח space do not draw nourishment from one another.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Sages know for certain that five seeds in six handbreadths do not draw nourishment from one another.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the משנה allows five different species in one 6×6 ערוגה. The reason is that the Sages have a tradition that, at this spacing, the plants do not pull food from each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem of כלאים comes from plants mixing and drawing nourishment from one another. The Sages' tradition says that at this arrangement and distance no such drawing happens. That is why the משנה's layout is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: They know for certain / it is an accepted tradition for them
The prohibition of planting mixed species together

steps.whyThisMatters: The whole permission of the משנה rests on this tradition. That is why the very next step asks how reliable such a tradition is.

phrases.english: And the Sages have an accepted tradition
do not draw nourishment from one another.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the previous discussion of how the five seeds are arranged in the bed by giving its underlying reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Five species within a six-טפח bed do not draw from each other, so there is no כלאים problem.

steps.title: Why can we rely on the Sages' tradition?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that this tradition of the Sages is a reliable, substantial matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that this thing which the Sages know for certain, that five in six [do not draw from each other], is a real matter?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source showing that we may build הלכה on the Sages' agricultural tradition. This sets up the next step, which brings a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is not whether the tradition is true in nature. It asks why the Torah lets us rely on it in a matter of איסור. The גמרא wants a scriptural basis for trusting this kind of inherited knowledge.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do we know?
It is a real / substantial matter

phrases.english: And from where do we know that this
that the Sages have as an accepted tradition

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the basis of the tradition just stated.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A scriptural source for relying on the Sages' tradition about planting distances.

steps.title: Do not cross the border set by the early generations
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reads 'לא תסיג גבול רעך אשר גבלו ראשונים' as a command not to change the planting limits that earlier generations set.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: What is the meaning of the verse 'Do not move your neighbor's boundary, which the early ones set'? It means: the boundary that the early ones set, do not move it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a פסוק. The Torah tells us not to move the 'boundaries' that earlier generations set, and these include the proper spacing for plants.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On its plain meaning the פסוק is about moving a land marker. רבי יוחנן reads it more widely, as respect for the limits fixed by the ראשונים. That gives Torah backing to the Sages' inherited measures, such as five species in six טפחים.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written?

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think this step is only about stealing land. Here the גמרא uses the פסוק as a source for trusting the planting measures of earlier generations.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said
What is that which is written:
the boundary that the early ones set

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by bringing a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'לא תסיג גבול' commands us to keep the limits set by the early generations, so their tradition is binding.

steps.title: Who are the early ones who set the boundaries?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'גבלו ראשונים' refers to: who set these boundaries?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks who the 'early ones' in the פסוק are. This sets up the next step, which identifies them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before we rely on their measures, we need to know who these ראשונים were and why their knowledge counts. The answer will show that they were real experts in the land.

keyTerms.meaning: They set the boundary / marked limits

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for clarification of a phrase in the פסוק just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Identification of the ראשונים whose boundaries we must not move.

steps.title: The people of שעיר were experts in farming the land
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן explains that 'יושבי הארץ' describes the children of שעיר as experts in which land is fit for olives, grapes, or figs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יונתן: What is the meaning of the verse 'These are the sons of שעיר החורי, the settlers of the land'? Does everyone else live in the sky?! Rather, it means they were experts in settling the land. They would say: this rod-length of land is good for olives, this rod-length for grapes, this rod-length for figs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא identifies the ראשונים as the children of שעיר החורי. It reads 'settlers of the land' as meaning they were experts in what each patch of land could grow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'יושבי הארץ' seem extra, because everyone lives on the land. So the פסוק must mean something special: these people knew the land well. They could look at a strip one rod long and say which crop it suited. Measures fixed by such experts are the kind of 'boundaries' we must not move.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it so that…? (opens a rhetorical question)
Experts in settling and farming the land
The full length of a measuring rod

phrases.english: What is that which is written
"These are the sons of Seir the Horite
in the settlement of the land,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ראשונים were the children of שעיר, experts in which land suits which crop.
steps.whatToRemember: Agricultural measures handed down from expert early generations count as 'boundaries' the Torah tells us not to move.

steps.title: The חורי smelled the land; the חוי tasted it
steps.stepSummary: The name חורי is read as 'smelling' the earth. רב פפא reads חוי as tasting the earth like a snake.
steps.simpleTranslation: And 'חורי' means that they smelled the land. And 'חוי': רב פפא said, that they would taste the land like a snake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds wordplays on the names of these peoples, showing how they tested the soil. חורי hints at smelling, and חוי hints at a snake that tastes the earth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חורי is linked to מריחים by swapping the letters ח and ר. חוי is linked to חויא, a snake, which eats dust. Both names stress how expert these peoples were with the land.

phrases.english: because they would taste the land

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the idea of the land experts through the meaning of their names.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The names חורי and חוי reflect how these peoples tested the soil by smelling and tasting it.

steps.title: Another meaning of חורי: freed of their property
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב reads חורי as 'בני חורין', people freed (stripped) of their possessions.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: 'חורי' means that they became 'free' (בני חורין) of their property.
steps.whatsHappening: A different אמורא gives another explanation of the name חורי. They were called this because they lost their lands and became 'free' of their property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to this view, חורי is not about smelling the soil. It is a nickname for a people who were driven out of their land, by the sons of עשו. Their real name was חוי, the tasters of the land.

keyTerms.meaning: Free people (here: freed of, stripped of)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different explanation of the name חורי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חורי means they were stripped of their possessions.

steps.title: The six handbreadths do not include the borders
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי rules that the 6×6 of the bed is measured inside, and the borders are extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said: The garden bed: its inside is six, not counting its borders.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the הלכה of the משנה and sets how the bed is measured. The six טפחים are the inner planting area only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think the border strips are part of the six טפחים. רב אסי says they are not. The planting space alone must be 6×6, and the borders are added on top, so the whole bed is larger.

phrases.english: A garden bed — its inside is six

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the aggadic side discussion and returns to the measurements of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 6×6 is the inner area; the borders are measured separately.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב אסי
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא also says the inside of the bed is six.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught so: A garden bed, its inside is six.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing as רב אסי, which supports his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'תוכה' (its inside) in the ברייתא shows that the measure is of the inner area. That matches רב אסי's ruling that the borders are not included.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (a ברייתא supports it)

phrases.english: A garden bed — its inside is six.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב אסי with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רב אסי's ruling that the six is measured inside the bed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that uses the word 'תוכה'.

steps.title: How wide are the borders?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how wide the borders of the bed are.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the borders are added outside the six, the גמרא asks how wide they are. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once we know the borders are extra, we need their width to know the full size of the bed.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows naturally from the ruling that the borders are extra.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The width of the bed's borders.

steps.title: The border is as wide as a foot
steps.stepSummary: Quoting a משנה, רבי יהודה says the border is the width of a foot.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: רבי יהודה says, the width is the full width of a foot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from a משנה. רבי יהודה sets the border's width at the width of a foot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A border is where a person walks to water the plants, so it needs to be as wide as a foot. The next step gives the source for this measure.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה

phrases.english: As we learned: Rabbi Yehuda says:
is like the full width of a foot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the border width.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The border is the width of a foot.

steps.title: The source: watering with your foot
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא, or רבי חנינא בר פפא, derives רבי יהודה's measure from 'והשקית ברגלך': a foot is a טפח, so the border is a טפח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said, and some say רבי חנינא בר פפא: What is רבי יהודה's reason? As it is written, 'And you water it with your foot like a vegetable garden.' Just as a foot is a handbreadth, so too a border is a handbreadth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the פסוק behind רבי יהודה's view. It turns the foot measurement into an exact number: one טפח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק connects watering a vegetable garden with the foot, because you walk along the border to water. The foot's width is a טפח, so the border must be one טפח. This tells us the full size of the bed: 6 inside plus the borders.

phrases.english: and some say Rabbi Ḥanina bar Pappa:
What is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda —
as it is written: "And you water with your foot
just as a foot is a handbreadth,
so too a border is also a handbreadth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the scriptural reason for רבי יהודה's measure.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The border of a bed is one טפח, learned from the width of the foot.
steps.whatToRemember: The bed is 6×6 טפחים inside, plus borders one טפח wide.

steps.title: The משנה is speaking of a lone bed in a ruin
steps.stepSummary: רב limits the משנה's five-species bed to a bed standing alone in a desolate area.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: The garden bed — we learned it about one in a ruin.
steps.whatsHappening: רב says the משנה's case is a single bed standing alone, with no other plantings around it. If it sits among other beds, planting five species is not allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Next to other beds, the species from neighboring beds would mix with this bed's plants. So the five-species permission works only when the bed is isolated, in a חורבה. This narrows the setting of the משנה without changing its rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A ruin / desolate area with no other plantings

phrases.english: we learned it regarding a ruin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new point about where the משנה's bed is located.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's five-species bed is a bed standing alone, not one among other beds.

steps.title: But there is still room in the corners
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב: if the bed stands alone, the empty corners could hold more species, so why only five?
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is the area of the corners!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב's explanation. In the משנה's layout the corners are left empty, so a lone bed could hold more than five species.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה puts four species along the sides and one in the middle, which leaves the corners open. If no other beds are nearby, more species could go in the corners. So why does the משנה stop at five?

phrases.english: But there is the space of the corners!

steps.kashyaTarget: רב's claim that the משנה speaks of a bed in a ruin.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A lone bed has free corners, so the משנה should allow more than five species.

steps.title: He fills the corners with the five species
steps.stepSummary: The school of רב answers that the case is where he extends the five species into the corners.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רב said in the name of רב: The case is where he fills the corners.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer is that in the משנה's case the person plants the five species all the way into the corners. That leaves no room for more species.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The corners are not empty in this case, because the rows of the five species reach into them. So it makes sense that the משנה counts only five.

phrases.english: The school of Rav said in the name of Rav:
It is where he fills the corners.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about the corners.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The corners stay empty, so more species could fit.
steps.terutzMaskana: The five species are planted into the corners, so no space is left.

steps.title: Why not plant outside instead of filling the corners?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes further: let him plant other species outside and not fill the corners inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him plant on the outside and not fill on the inside!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer. Why would the משנה describe filling the corners, when a person could leave them and plant more species outside? The answer to this challenge comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the goal is to grow as many species as possible, filling the corners seems wasteful. Since the bed is in a ruin, there is open space outside where more species could be planted. So the answer 'he fills the corners' does not seem to explain why the משנה stops at five.

phrases.english: So let him plant on the outside
and not fill in from the inside!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer that he fills the corners.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the case is where he fills the corners.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He could leave the corners and plant more species outside, so filling the corners does not explain why the משנה stops at five.
